gloss: (northern, 1/5) I'm telling you (standard: σου λέω); northern accusative for the indirect object

example.en: I'm telling you, I'm not coming tonight.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (northern, 1/5) he/she told me (standard: μου είπε); but 'με είπε βλάκα' = he called me an idiot is standard

example.el: Με είπε να περιμένω στην Καμάρα.
example.en: He told me to wait at the Arch.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (northern, 1/5) you don't say! what are you telling me? (standard: τι μου λες;)

example.en: You don't say! He's getting married?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (Thessaloniki, 1/5) you're kidding me! (Athens: πλάκα μου κάνεις; / σοβαρολογείς;)

example.el: Πλάκα με κάνεις! Έκλεισε το μαγαζί;
example.en: You're kidding me! The shop closed?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (northern, 1/5) give me (standard: δώσε μου)

example.en: Give me a minute.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (strict northern rural, 1/5) = σε λέω, with unstressed vowels raised; the stereotype of village Macedonian/Thessalian speech

example.en: I'm telling you, he didn't come.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (northern rural pronunciation) = παιδί, child; unstressed e raised to i

example.en: The child is asleep.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: 'thick l': the dark, velarised [ɫ] of Macedonia and Thessaloniki, a favourite target of Athenian imitation

example.en: She imitates my thick l.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (linguistics) 'deafening': raising and loss of unstressed vowels typical of northern Greek dialects

example.el: Η κώφωση είναι το βασικό γνώρισμα των βόρειων ιδιωμάτων.
example.en: Vowel reduction is the main feature of the northern dialects.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (colloquial, 1/5; northern) supposedly, as if, 'and-like' (= δήθεν, τάχα, και καλά); from Turkish demek 'that is to say'

example.el: Ήρθε ντεμέκ άρρωστος, αλλά τον είδα στην παραλία.
example.en: He came in supposedly ill, but I saw him on the seafront.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 2/5) fakery, pretentiousness, posing (from ντεμέκ)

example.en: The event was pure pretence.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (colloquial, Thessaloniki) you know (= ξέρεις), filler

example.en: It was closed, you know?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (Thessaloniki) go! imperative of πάω (= πήγαινε); elsewhere usually 'they go'

example.en: Go and get some bread.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (Thessaloniki, 1/5) sure, of course (= Athenian αμέ)

example.en: – Are you coming? – Sure!

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (Thessaloniki) it's turned cold (Athens: έπιασε/έβαλε κρύο)

example.en: It's turned cold, take a jacket.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (northern colloquial) three hundred (= τριακόσια)

example.en: It cost me three hundred euros.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (colloquial, Macedonia) a flat tyre; έπαθα φούιτ = I got a flat (Athens: μ' έπιασε λάστιχο); from French fuite

example.en: I got a flat on Egnatia Street.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (colloquial, Athens/standard) I've got a flat tyre

example.en: I got a flat on Kifisias Avenue.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (Thessaloniki and other cities) the city bus (Athens: λεωφορείο)

example.el: Πήρα το αστικό για το κέντρο.
example.en: I took the city bus into town.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (colloquial, Thessaloniki) fuchsia, hot pink (= φούξια); indeclinable

example.en: She wore a hot-pink dress.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (regional) Athens/south: a meat skewer (σουβλάκι στο ξυλάκι); Thessaloniki: a drinking straw

example.en: Two pork skewers, please. (Athens)

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (regional sense) in Athens also the whole pita wrap (ένα σουβλάκι γύρο); in Thessaloniki strictly the skewer

example.en: Shall we go for souvlaki?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (Athens) the pita wrap, e.g. τυλιχτό γύρο χοιρινό

example.el: Ένα τυλιχτό γύρο με απ' όλα.
example.en: A gyros wrap with everything.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (northern colloquial) gyros in pita

example.en: Two gyros pitas for the road.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (northern way of ordering) a gyros pita

example.en: Shall we go for a gyros pita?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (regional sense) in Athenian souvlaki shops often a fizzy lemon soft drink; in Thessaloniki real lemonade

example.en: Here 'lemonade' means the soft drink.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (regional sense) in Thessaloniki: feta by default; in Athens any (often yellow) cheese

example.en: A Greek salad with lots of feta. (Thessaloniki)

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: kasseri cheese; in Thessaloniki the word for any yellow cheese

example.en: A toastie with yellow cheese.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (Thessaloniki) any creamy mayonnaise- or yogurt-based salad or dip; elsewhere 'ointment'

example.el: Βάλε και λίγη αλοιφή στο πιάτο.
example.en: Put a bit of creamy dip on the plate.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: filo pie with custard (or cheese, mince, spinach); Thessaloniki's breakfast icon; in Athens assumed to be with cream

example.en: A custard bougatsa with cinnamon.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: 'cream or cheese?' the Thessaloniki bougatsa question, a north/south joke in itself

example.en: – One bougatsa. – Cream or cheese?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: the sesame bread ring (Athenian name; in Thessaloniki just κουλούρι)

example.el: Πήρα ένα κουλούρι Θεσσαλονίκης στο μετρό.
example.en: I grabbed a sesame ring at the metro.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: iced shaken instant coffee, improvised at the Thessaloniki International Fair in 1957; γλυκός/μέτριος/σκέτος

example.en: A medium-sweet frappé with milk.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: a meze restaurant serving tsipouro, each carafe with a small dish

example.el: Πάμε σε ένα τσιπουράδικο στο Καπάνι.
example.en: Let's go to a tsipouro place in Kapani.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: let's go out for tsipouro and mezedes

example.en: Shall we go out for tsipouro on Friday?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 1-2/5; northern) an Athenian or southerner, from χάμω 'down there'

example.en: I'm going down to the southerners for work.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 2/5) 'bougatsa-eater': teasing name for a Thessalonian

example.el: Ήρθαν οι μπουγατσοφάγοι για το ματς.
example.en: The bougatsa-eaters have come for the match.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 1/5) 'frappé-city': jokey name for Thessaloniki

example.el: Ανέβηκα στη φραπεδούπολη για το Σαββατοκύριακο.
example.en: I went up to frappé-city for the weekend.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (ironic, 1/5) the Athens–Thessaloniki rivalry; any petty, pointless feud

example.el: Άσ' τα, ο καβγάς της μπουγάτσας ξανά.
example.en: Forget it, the bougatsa feud again.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: the co-capital: journalistic name for Thessaloniki (can sound ironic)

example.en: Rain in the co-capital.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: Thessaloniki (popular, affectionate name)

example.en: I miss Saloniki.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: a Thessalonian (fem. Σαλονικιά)

example.el: Είναι Σαλονικιός, το καταλαβαίνεις από το λ.
example.en: He's from Thessaloniki; you can tell from his l.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: 'the bride of the Thermaic Gulf': poetic name for Thessaloniki

example.el: Η νύφη του Θερμαϊκού στο ηλιοβασίλεμα.
example.en: The bride of the Thermaic at sunset.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: the Arch of Galerius in Thessaloniki, the city's classic meeting point (τα λέμε στην Καμάρα)

example.el: Τα λέμε στην Καμάρα στις εννιά.
example.en: See you at the Arch at nine.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: I go down to Athens (northern perspective; Athenians ανεβαίνουν Θεσσαλονίκη)

example.en: Tomorrow I'm going down to Athens for work.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: 'from Lamia upwards': jokey line dividing northern from southern Greece

example.el: Από τη Λαμία και πάνω όλοι λένε «σε λέω».
example.en: From Lamia upwards everyone says 'se leo'.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 2/5) a pretentious arty intellectual, culture snob (fem. κουλτουριάρα)

example.en: Shall we go to the cinema with the arty crowd?

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 2/5) a woolly, obscure pseudo-intellectual

example.en: He talked for an hour like a muddled pseudo-intellectual.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: Athens district; byword for posh, trendy and expensive

example.el: Καφές στο Κολωνάκι; Θα μας μαδήσουν!
example.en: Coffee in Kolonaki? They'll fleece us!

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: Athens district of students, bookshops, bars, left/anarchist politics and riot police (neuter plural)

example.en: We went out for beers in Exarchia.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: the northern suburbs of Athens (Kifisia, Ekali, Psychiko): wealth stereotype, abbreviated ΒΠ

example.el: Μεγάλωσε στα βόρεια προάστια, ιδιωτικό σχολείο και τέτοια.
example.en: He grew up in the northern suburbs, private school and all that.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 2-3/5) a show-off lad with a souped-up car or bike and loud music

example.el: Πέρασε ένας κάγκουρας με την εξάτμιση στο φουλ.
example.en: A boy racer went by with his exhaust roaring.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (colloquial, 1/5) a capital-dweller, Athenian (seen from the provinces; can imply arrogance)

example.el: Ήρθαν οι πρωτευουσιάνοι και τα ξέρουν όλα.
example.en: The big-city people have arrived and know it all.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: Athens-centrism: treating Athens as the whole country (northern complaint)

example.el: Ο αθηνοκεντρισμός των καναλιών μας τρελαίνει.
example.en: The TV channels' Athens-centrism drives us mad.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: I go into central Athens (downtown)

example.en: On Saturday we're going downtown.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 2/5) an Olympiakos fan (lit. anchovy, from the Piraeus port); rivals' nickname, often self-adopted

example.en: The whole office are Olympiakos fans.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (slang, 2/5) a Panathinaikos fan (from βαζελίνη); rivals' nickname

example.en: The Panathinaikos fans partied all night.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (offensive, 3/5) 'harem lady': rivals' jibe at AEK and its fans (Constantinopolitan roots)

example.en: They were chanting 'harem girls' in the stands.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (offensive, 4/5) slur for PAOK fans and northerners in general; an ethnic insult, not banter

example.el: Μη λες «βούλγαρους» τους Σαλονικιούς, είναι προσβολή.
example.en: Don't call Thessalonians 'Bulgarians', it's an insult.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (offensive, 3/5) mocking spelling of ΠΑΟΚ used by rival fans

example.en: They wrote 'BAOK' on the wall.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: 'the Legend': Olympiakos fans' name for their club

example.en: Legend, you're my life! (chant)

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: the shamrock: emblem and nickname of Panathinaikos

example.en: Panathinaikos won the derby.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: the double-headed eagle: emblem and nickname of PAOK (ο Δικέφαλος του Βορρά) and of AEK

example.el: Ο Δικέφαλος του Βορρά κέρδισε στην Τούμπα.
example.en: PAOK won at Toumba.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: a fan of Aris Thessaloniki

example.en: The Aris fans filled Harilaou.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (football sense) a stadium gate, hence the organised fan group behind it (Θύρα 7, Θύρα 13, Θύρα 4)

example.el: Η Θύρα 4 τραγουδούσε όλο το ματς.
example.en: Gate 4 sang the whole match.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: (colloquial, 2/5) we thrashed you (lit. we took your underpants)

example.en: We thrashed you yesterday!

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude

gloss: what team do you support? (standard getting-to-know-you question)

example.en: – What team are you? – PAOK, of course.

source: colloquial lexicon; entry written by Claude
